chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Ammar ibn Marwan said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about al-ghulul (booty taken by a leader or official), so he said: 'Everything that is taken (ghull) by the Imam is suht (consumption of unlawful wealth), and eating the wealth of the orphan and its like is suht. And suht has many types, among them are the wages of the faqirah (prostitutes/deep sinners), the price of wine, nabidh, and the intoxicant, and riba (usury) after clear proof. As for al-rishwah (bribery) in judgment, then that is kufr (disbelief) by the Great God and by His Messenger.'

key_terms.اَلنَّبِيذِ: Nabidh (fermented drink made from dates or grapes)
key_terms.اَلْغُلُولِ: Booty or wealth taken by a leader or official, often implying excess or unlawfulness
key_terms.اَلْفَوَاجِرِ: Those who commit major sins, often referring to prostitutes
key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Consumption of unlawful wealth or sustenance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-ghulul and how does it differ from bribery in judgment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) expands the concept of *al-ghulul* beyond mere booty seizure to encompass any unlawfully acquired wealth, categorizing it as *suht* (consumable impurity). He provides specific examples such as wages of sinners and prices of intoxicants, while elevating judicial bribery (*arshah*) to the status of major disbelief (*kufr*), highlighting its severity in Shia jurisprudence.
